rationale: Vedolizumab's role extends from first-line biologic selection in naïve UC patients (AGA 2020, ranked alongside infliximab above adalimumab) to maintenance after cyclosporine rescue in severe UC (ACG 2019), broadening vedolizumab's clinical positioning from initial biologic choice through post-rescue maintenance in advanced disease.

Vedolizumab maintenance after cyclosporine rescue (ACG 2019) logically depends on the rescue therapy itself: AGA 2020 defines the rescue step — infliximab or cyclosporine for steroid-refractory ASUC — which must precede the vedolizumab maintenance that ACG 2019 recommends, forming a sequential treatment pathway from rescue through maintenance.

The budesonide MMX second-line recommendation for 5-ASA-refractory left-sided UC (ACG 2019) depends on first-line 5-ASA optimization strategies: ECCO 2022 recommends combined oral plus topical 5-ASA as an escalation over oral alone, and budesonide MMX only enters the algorithm after such 5-ASA optimization strategies have been exhausted without adequate response.

The systemic steroids recommendation for 5-ASA failure (ACG 2019) logically depends on first-line oral 5-ASA induction at ≥2 g/day (ECCO 2022): systemic steroids are reserved for patients who have failed initial 5-ASA therapy, making the first-line induction recommendation a prerequisite in the treatment algorithm.

For distal colitis, the step to systemic steroids after 5-ASA failure (ACG 2019) depends on first-line topical 5-ASA induction at ≥1 g/day (ECCO 2022): systemic steroids enter the treatment algorithm only after topical 5-ASA, the recommended first-line therapy for distal disease, has proven inadequate.

Systemic steroids for 5-ASA failure (ACG 2019) depend on prior 5-ASA optimization: ECCO 2022's combined oral plus topical 5-ASA recommendation represents an escalated 5-ASA strategy that should be attempted before declaring 5-ASA failure and progressing to systemic steroids, placing combined 5-ASA as an intermediate step in the treatment pathway.

The recommendation against switching 5-ASA formulations (ACG 2019) complements the oral 5-ASA induction dosing guidance (ECCO 2022): together they define both what to do (induction at ≥2 g/day) and what to avoid (unnecessary formulation switching), providing comprehensive 5-ASA prescribing guidance for UC induction.

The counsel against switching 5-ASA formulations (ACG 2019) complements the topical 5-ASA dosing recommendation for distal colitis induction (ECCO 2022): while ECCO specifies the appropriate topical dose (≥1 g/day), ACG advises against the common clinical practice of switching between formulations, together delivering complete prescribing guidance for topical 5-ASA in distal UC.

The recommendation against formulation switching (ACG 2019) complements the oral 5-ASA maintenance dosing guidance (ECCO 2022, ≥2 g/day): together they define appropriate maintenance dosing and counsel against the common practice of interchanging 5-ASA formulations, providing comprehensive oral 5-ASA stewardship for UC maintenance.

The advice against switching 5-ASA formulations (ACG 2019) complements the topical 5-ASA maintenance recommendation for distal UC (ECCO 2022): ECCO establishes the role of topical 5-ASA in distal UC maintenance, while ACG's advice against switching formulations supports consistent, uninterrupted topical maintenance therapy.

The recommendation to add budesonide MMX for partial 5-ASA response (ACG 2019) logically depends on first-line oral 5-ASA induction (ECCO 2022): budesonide MMX augmentation is only indicated after 5-ASA induction at ≥2 g/day has been tried and produced only a partial response, making first-line 5-ASA a necessary prerequisite.

For distal UC, the budesonide MMX add-on for partial 5-ASA response (ACG 2019) depends on first-line topical 5-ASA induction at ≥1 g/day (ECCO 2022): budesonide MMX augmentation is reserved for patients who have achieved only partial response to initial topical 5-ASA therapy for distal colitis.

Budesonide MMX augmentation for partial 5-ASA response (ACG 2019) depends on prior 5-ASA optimization: ECCO 2022's combined oral plus topical 5-ASA recommendation represents an escalated 5-ASA strategy for rectosigmoid and more extensive disease; budesonide MMX is the next step when even combined 5-ASA yields only partial response.

The recommendation against concomitant 5-ASA with anti-TNF maintenance (ACG 2019) complements the anti-TNF induction recommendation for moderate-severe UC (ECCO 2022): ECCO establishes anti-TNF as standard induction therapy for moderate-severe disease, while ACG clarifies that adding 5-ASA to anti-TNF maintenance provides no additional benefit, together defining the complete anti-TNF prescribing framework from initiation through maintenance without unnecessary polypharmacy.
